text_to_speech: Hapag-Lloyd just finished the first quarter of 2017 and joining me now here in the Fleet Support Center is Rolf Habben Jansen, the CEO of Hapag-Lloyd. How satisfied are you with the results? The results of the first quarter have been a mixed bag. Volume was strong, there are some improvements in rate but not as much as we would like and bunker costs went actually up quite a lot. What impact had the latest developments in freight rates and bunker prices on the results? Well, you always see when bunker cost goes up it takes a little bit of time before you see that reflected in the freight rates. So in the first quarter we definitely see the effects of higher bunker costs but not yet the full effects of the increase in freight rates which we actually expect to see in the second and especially the third and fourth quarter onwards. What kind of further development do you expect with regard to freight rates and bunker prices? Well, today the market is quite strong. I mean, volume is developing well and we believe that the freight rates will recover further which is also not illogical after they had been declining for such a long time. What main activities did you focus on in the last quarter and what are the priorities for the next months? Well, of course for us it was important in the first quarter to continue working on the project with UASC that is now very close to completion and that also means that in Q2 and Q3 we will be very much focused on the integration apart from, of course, continuing to offer good service for our customers and negotiating best possible rates also for the remain of 2017 and hopefully already into 2018 as well. What are your expectations for the rest of the year for the industry and for Hapag-Lloyd? Well, as far as we can see it right now, the outlook is actually fairly positive. Supply and demand are getting closer and closer together. We see that the contracts that we close today generally have better rates than what we have seen before and I believe that we are well prepared for the integration, so from that perspective I’m cautiously optimistic when looking into the remain of 2017. Thank you Rolf Habben Jansen, the CEO of Hapag-Lloyd and thank you for watching.

In a short interview, Hapag-Lloyd CEO Rolf Habben Jansen talks about the result of the first quarter 2017, his main priorities in the next months as well as his expectations for the rest of the year – for Hapag-Lloyd and the whole industry.
